newsitem.title: UK: Tate exceptionals prompt profit downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Tate exceptionals prompt profit downgrades.

text.p: Tate and Lyle Plc's move to take big exceptional charges for reorganisation in its first half results plus disappointment at its overall performance prompted investment analysts to downgrade profit forecast for the current year.
Analysts said ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett had cut its 1997 forecast to 240 million stg from 255 million.
The international sweetener and starches group made an exceptional charge of 83.2 million stg to cover a reorganisation of its North American activities, plus asset write downs.
Analysts said the size of the charge was unexpected as was a 10.9 million stg loss in Russia from sugar trading activities.
"There were one or two unknown items in the numbers, but generally they delivered what they had pointed to at update meetings back at the end of the first half," said one food manufacturing analyst.
Analysts were more positive on the longer term outlook for the company under new chief executive Larry Pillard, who took control last November.

"Larry Pillard is a strong manager and he's addressing the issues robustly," said Sally Jones at Credit Lyonnais Securities. She is cutting her current year forecast to 230 million stg from 248 million.
Analysts agreed that the rest of 1997 would be difficult because of the squeeze on profits at Tate's corn wet milling business in the U.S., traditionally a big driver of profitability.
Although this proved resilient in tough market conditions analysts said it would take a while for it to return to anything like its historic levels of contibution to earnings.
